exposure: Maternal age (40 years or older vs. 20-30 years)
maternal age of 40 years or more
cohort: 797 women aged 40 years or older and 18,802 women aged 20-30 years who delivered at Chiang Mai University Hospital, Thailand, between 2002 and 2012
finding: Women aged 40 years or older had significantly higher rates of medical complications, cesarean sections, preterm deliveries, and fetal growth restriction compared to women aged 20-30 years.
mod_finding: This study found that cesarean section rates were significantly higher in women aged 40 years or older compared to those aged 20-30 years.
